clue.text: Model drawing by engineer is profitable

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a common crossword engineer

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so the letters of drawing are reshaped

explanation.surface: A design sketched by an engineer turns out to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun describing the drawing, but it is the anagram signal; its letters make WARDING, and 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewarding work pays off, so it is a synonym for profitable or worthwhile.

clue.text: Incumbent stops before right page

indicators.note: the clergyman's word halts before reaching its final right letter

parts.note: a rector is the incumbent of a parish

explanation.surface: A vicar halts before the right-hand page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops before right' says RECTOR stops short of its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A recto is the right-hand page of an open book.

clue.text: Several holding up victory with appeal

indicators.note: in a down answer the several piece sits below and supports the victory

parts.note: a win is a victory
some means several

explanation.surface: A few people supporting a win have charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' places SOME beneath WIN in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming or attractive, having appeal.

clue.text: Recited fluently and danced away

definitions.meaning: to reel off a list is to say it quickly and easily
to reel is to dance a reel, and off means away

explanation.definitionFit: Reeling off is rattling off words; reeling off is also dancing a reel away.

clue.text: Sick generation's bad manners

parts.note: ill means sick
breeding is the producing of offspring, a generation

explanation.surface: An unhealthy generation is rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill breeding is a lack of good upbringing, shown in rudeness.

clue.text: College servant in pain

definitions.meaning: to give someone ... is to cause them pain

explanation.walkthrough: A GYP is a manservant at Cambridge or Durham colleges; 'give someone gyp' is British slang for hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British: a Cambridge college attendant and informal pain.

clue.text: Decomposing matter affronts us with a smell

indicators.note: read as 'a-fronts', it says the smell stands at the front of the word us

parts.note: a hum is slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Rotting stuff offends us by its stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affronts' looks like 'offends' but splits as 'a-fronts': the smell goes in front. HUM is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is the dark organic soil material formed from rotting leaves and plants.

clue.text: Governor has welcome for swell

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of a governor
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: The governor receives a greeting worth getting excited about.
explanation.definitionFit: A heave is the rise and fall of the sea, a swell.

clue.text: Sovereign's Parade contains nothing new

indicators.note: the parade word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a march is a parade
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The royal parade has nothing new to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts O and N inside MARCH; the 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a king or queen, a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Forced to wed, Sara's taken to drink

indicators.note: forced means made to change, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Sara, pushed into marriage, has turned to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forced' rearranges TO WED SARA; 'taken to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated water, a drink.

clue.text: Hide to study aquatic mammal, say

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: say signals that the following word is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a hiding place to watch a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb meaning to study; 'say' marks a word only heard, so the spelling may differ.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to hide it from view, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Page was first to grab girl, as intended

indicators.note: the leader's word takes hold of the girl's name, putting it inside

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A page boy got in first to seize a girl, just as he meant to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' puts the girl inside the word for 'was first', giving LANNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something planned happened by design, exactly as intended.

clue.text: In Australia one finds fresh air

parts.note: Oz is a familiar nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: Someone discovers clean air down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used informally, especially at the seaside, for bracing fresh air.

clue.text: Horses here making foul noise?

parts.note: rotten means foul or putrid
a row is a loud din

explanation.surface: Are horses the cause of this disgusting racket?
explanation.walkthrough: ROTTEN ROW is a sandy track in London's Hyde Park used for horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten Row is the bridleway in Hyde Park, so it is a place where horses are found.

clue.text: Composer restricted by time factor as an arranger of movements

indicators.note: the composer is hemmed in by the other letters around him

parts.note: an agent or factor acts for another
Ravel is the French composer

explanation.surface: A composer is limited by time in arranging movements of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' looks musical, next to a composer, but means people's journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel agent arranges people's journeys, their movements.

clue.text: On a car this would give a prompt signal

definitions.text: On a car this would give a prompt signal

parts.words: On a car this would give a prompt signal
parts.note: the letter it sounds like, added to car, names an unmarked police vehicle; alone it is a signal to an actor

explanation.surface: Something fitted to a vehicle flashes a quick warning.
explanation.walkthrough: A Q-car is a British police car disguised as an ordinary one; the word for the letter Q is a theatrical prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's cue is the prompt telling them to speak or enter.

clue.text: Slips, could one say, on top of tank collecting water

indicators.note: in a down light the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: slips are cricket fielders who catch, so one might call them catch men

indicators.note: only the first letter of tank is taken

explanation.surface: Slip fielders stand on a tank that holds water.
explanation.walkthrough: Slips are close-catching fielders in cricket. 'could one say' admits CATCHMEN is a coined description.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchment is an area or system for gathering rainwater.

clue.text: Obvious contradiction

definitions.meaning: a case easily settled is plain and clear
opposites, so the phrase contradicts itself

explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is straightforward, and the two words also cancel each other out.

clue.text: After dance, glare appears to fade

indicators.note: the glare comes after the dance

parts.note: a disco is a dance
to lour is to scowl or glare

explanation.surface: After a night out dancing, bright lights seem dimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To discolour is to lose colour, to fade or stain.

clue.text: Good husbandry is first, then work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or rework it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Careful farming comes first, and then the labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges IS, FIRST and THEN; the comma is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry in its older sense means careful management of resources, which is thrift.

clue.text: Deep cut's opening in tyre

indicators.note: the cut's first letter is placed inside the tyre

parts.note: a radial is a type of tyre

indicators.note: only the first letter of cut is taken

explanation.surface: A deep gash opens up in a tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' gives C; 'in' puts it inside RADIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical means thorough or going to the root, so deep-seated.

clue.text: Sweep the board within limits

indicators.note: only what lies inside the outer letters of board is taken

explanation.surface: Someone wins every prize, inside the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep the board' looks like a phrase, but 'Sweep' is the definition and 'the' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a long oar used in rowing boats.

clue.text: Old jalopy — one with a new switching instrument

parts.note: a jalopy is an old car
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: switching means the two letters swap places

explanation.surface: An old banger with a new gearstick makes music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' swaps A and N to give NA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.

clue.text: Hay distributed round exotic garden shrub

indicators.note: the hay letters surround the other group
spread out, so the letters of hay are rearranged
foreign or unusual, so the word garden is jumbled

explanation.surface: Hay is spread around a foreign shrub in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden shrub' wants to be the definition, but 'garden' is fodder for the second anagram, signalled by 'exotic'; 'round' sets it inside the scrambled hay.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a common flowering bush grown in gardens.

clue.text: See eye to eye with Silver about rope's end

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: only the last letter of rope is taken

explanation.surface: Two people agree with Long John Silver about a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is an idiom for being in agreement.

clue.text: Mate wearing very large jewels

indicators.note: the friend puts on the size label like clothing, so it goes outside

parts.note: OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize
a pal is a mate or friend

explanation.surface: A friend is wearing enormous gems.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing size label; 'wearing' means the mate is dressed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones, so they are jewels.

clue.text: Write letters correctly in term

definitions.meaning: to put the letters of a word in the right order
a period or term of time

explanation.definitionFit: Spelling is writing letters correctly; a spell is also a period of time.

clue.text: Passage that is short, but about right

indicators.note: the word for but goes around the right letter

parts.note: except and but both mean 'other than'

explanation.surface: A passage is brief, but more or less accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside EXCEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract taken from a longer text.

clue.text: Contraction of credit discussed

indicators.note: discussed means talked about, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: buying on tick is buying on credit

explanation.surface: A shrinking of credit is talked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary muscle contraction or twitch.

clue.text: Key incentive for arousing passion

parts.note: E is a musical key
a motive is a reason or incentive

explanation.surface: An important stimulus serves to stir up feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language is designed to arouse strong feeling.

clue.text: What veils the bride, a length to pull back after the union

indicators.note: the length comes after the union in the answer

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union

indicators.note: pulling back means the word for a length is read backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A bride's veil is pulled back after the wedding ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pull back' turns the length backwards into LLE. 'Union' suggests a wedding but is a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is the fine net fabric used for bridal veils.

clue.text: Animal king initially waking everyone vocally with a shrill howl

parts.note: a cat is an animal
ER is Elizabeth Regina, used here loosely for a monarch

indicators.note: the first letter of waking only is wanted
vocally signals that the word for everyone is only heard, spelt differently

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A cat wakes the whole household with a piercing yowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocally' says ALL is sounded and written AUL; ER usually means queen, here a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is a screeching cry like that of cats at night.
